subject: pyrosome
title: A Glowing 60-Foot Tube Drifts Through the Sea, and It's Thousands of Animals

scenes.text: This glowing 60-foot tube is alive. And it isn't one animal.
A pyrosome. Thousands of creatures a few millimetres long, fused into one hollow sock, open at one end.
Each one pumps water through itself for food. Together, those tiny jets push the whole tube along.
In the dark it glows blue-green, waves of light rolling down the colony, visible 100 feet away.
The giants are wide enough to swim inside. One diver found a dead penguin trapped in one.
Every member is a clone, budding off the last. In theory the tube never has to die. Pyrosome means fire body.

description:
A pyrosome is a floating colony of thousands of tiny tunicates, each a few millimetres long, fused into a hollow gelatinous tube. Giant ones reach about 60 feet, wide enough for divers to swim inside.
Each animal filters water for food, and the combined jets move the colony. It glows pale blue-green, visible for tens of metres, and the members bud as clones, so a colony can in theory keep growing indefinitely. The name means fire body.
Would you swim into one? Comment below.
first_comment: In 2017 pyrosomes showed up in unheard-of numbers along the US West Coast, as far north as Alaska, and nobody knows why. Which ocean oddity should we cover next?
